title: Postgres: books load matches the source
summary: Loads the Gutenberg book text files into the Postgres table books and proves the table matches the source files: every file present, row count equal to what OpenETL reported, and real book text inside.

steps.title: Empty the books table
steps.explain: Starts from a clean slate so every row found later was written by this run.

steps.title: Count the source .txt files
steps.explain: Counts the input files so the result can be checked against a known number.

steps.title: Read sample rows of books (Before)
steps.explain: Shows the table before the run: it was just dropped, so there is nothing to read.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, sequence_index, left(text, 50) AS text_start FROM books ORDER BY source_filename, sequence_index LIMIT 5

steps.title: Run the pg_books pipeline
steps.explain: Runs the real pipeline. Everything below checks what it produced.

steps.title: Job finished with status COMPLETED
steps.explain: A finished job should say COMPLETED, not PARTIAL or FAILED.

steps.title: Job reported no warnings
steps.explain: Any warning means something was skipped or went wrong along the way.

steps.title: Job processed every source file
steps.explain: The number of files OpenETL read must equal the files on disk.

steps.title: Read distinct source files in the books table
steps.explain: Counts how many different source files landed in the table.

steps.title: Every source file is present in the table
steps.explain: No source file may be missing from the table.

steps.title: Read row count of the books table
steps.explain: The real number of rows in the table.

steps.title: Row count equals the records OpenETL reported
steps.explain: What OpenETL says it wrote must equal what the database holds.

steps.title: Count pg1342.txt rows that mention 'Pride and Prejudice'
steps.explain: Looks for known text from one book to prove real content arrived.

args.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM books WHERE source_filename='pg1342.txt' AND text ILIKE '%Pride and Prejudice%'

steps.title: pg1342.txt text contains 'Pride and Prejudice'
steps.explain: At least one row of that book must contain its title.

steps.title: Read sample rows of books (After)
steps.explain: Shows the same read after the run so the change is visible.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, sequence_index, left(text, 50) AS text_start FROM books ORDER BY source_filename, sequence_index LIMIT 5
